title: Look East to Act East

cards.h: Where South Asia meets the Pacific
cards.b:
India's turn to the East began in 1991. The Cold War ended, the Soviet Union fell, and India needed new markets and partners. East and Southeast Asia were the fastest growing region in the world.

The shift from Look East (a mostly economic policy) to Act East (2014, a strategic and security policy) is one of the most asked topics in this part of Paper II. It links to ASEAN, the Indo-Pacific, the Quad and the Northeast.

Key phrase for answers: ASEAN centrality. India says ASEAN must remain at the middle of the regional architecture.

cards.h: From Look East to Act East
cards.b:
Look East had phases: first a focus on ASEAN trade (1991–2002), then widening to East Asia, Japan, Korea and Australia, and a security dimension (joint exercises, maritime talks).

Act East adds action: faster delivery, a focus on connectivity, the Northeast, and defence cooperation. Modi announced it at the 12th ASEAN–India Summit in Nay Pyi Taw (November 2014). The Delhi Commemorative Summit (January 2018) saw all ten ASEAN leaders as Republic Day chief guests.

• ASEAN–India: Treaty of Amity and Cooperation accession (2003). Free Trade in Goods (signed 2009, in force January 2010), Services and Investment (in force July 2015).
  • AITIGA review: India wants the ASEAN–India Trade in Goods Agreement revised because of a large trade deficit (about $44 billion in 2023-24; total trade about $122 billion). The review had not concluded as of 2026.
  • East Asia Summit (EAS): India a founding member (2005). It now has 18 members.
  • Mekong–Ganga Cooperation (2000) and BIMSTEC link the sub-regions.
  • RCEP: India walked out in November 2019.
  • Newcomer: Timor-Leste became ASEAN's 11th member in October 2025.

Philippines chairs ASEAN in 2026.

The Northeast is the heart of Act East: 98% of its borders are international, and it connects India to Myanmar and Bangladesh.

  • Kaladan Multi-Modal Project and India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway (see the previous lesson).
  • Agartala–Akhaura rail and Chattogram port access, via Bangladesh.
  • Japan's Act East Forum funds roads and power in the Northeast.
  • Digital and air links: UPI with Singapore (2023) and direct flights.

Obstacles: conflict in Myanmar, delays, the closed Myanmar border, and fewer land links via Bangladesh after 2024. Critics say Act East needs less rhetoric and more roads.

India's defence ties in Southeast Asia have grown fast:

  • Vietnam: a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2016). India offered $500 million for defence purchases and trains submarine crews.
  • Philippines: the first export of the BrahMos missile (a $375 million deal signed in January 2022).
  • Indonesia: President Prabowo was chief guest at Republic Day 2025; BrahMos talks followed.
  • Singapore: naval exercise SIMBEX; a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2024.
  • Malaysia, Thailand: exercises and defence talks.

India sees the Indo-Pacific as one space and backs the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP, 2019). In November 2019 Modi announced the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI). Also on freedom of navigation, India backs the 2016 South China Sea arbitration ruling in favour of the Philippines.

cards.h: Two ways to read the East
cards.b:
C. Raja Mohan, Samudra Manthan (2012)

The Indian and Pacific Oceans are becoming one strategic theatre. India must act as a maritime power. Act East is part of that.

Amitav Acharya, Constructing a Security Community in Southeast Asia (2001)

The 'ASEAN way' of consultation, consensus and non-interference created norms that kept the region at peace. It is a constructivist reading that explains why ASEAN centrality matters.

Realists see Act East as balancing China. Constructivists stress shared norms and identity (cultural links such as Buddhism and the Ramayana traditions). Liberals focus on trade and institutions.

• Japan: the anchor partner (see the earlier lesson): the Special Strategic and Global Partnership of 2014.
  • South Korea: a Special Strategic Partnership (2015) and a CEPA (2010). Samsung and Hyundai are big investors. Korea's 'New Southern Policy' meets Act East.
  • Australia: a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2020), the ECTA trade deal (in force December 2022), and the Quad. Talks on a fuller CECA continued.
  • Pacific Islands: the Forum for India–Pacific Islands Cooperation (FIPIC) was started in 2014 at Suva.
  • Taiwan: unofficial ties, with a focus on semiconductors, through economic and cultural offices.

The Act East label therefore covers more than ASEAN. It extends the Indian reach from the Bay of Bengal to the Pacific. It is also a counter to China's presence in the same space.

India is a dialogue partner, not a member, of the main ASEAN economic structures. China is ASEAN's top trading partner; India is far behind. The Indian economy's limited integration into East Asian supply chains is a handicap.

Supporters point out that India now matters in ASEAN's security thinking and that bilateral partnerships (Vietnam, Philippines, Singapore, Indonesia) are growing.

• Renegotiate the ASEAN trade agreement and tackle non-tariff barriers.
  • Complete the Northeast's land and river links and keep the Sittwe route alive.
  • Use Malabar, the Quad and bilateral partnerships to support freedom of navigation.
  • Expand defence exports (BrahMos, Akash, patrol vessels).
  • Keep ASEAN centrality while joining minilaterals.

Example: India reached out to ASEAN at the 2025–26 summits while US tariffs rose. Diversification towards ASEAN and Japan was a clear theme.

"How does the Act East Policy differ from Look East? Examine its achievements." (typical)
"Discuss the importance of ASEAN to India's Indo-Pacific strategy." (typical)
"India's Northeast is the gateway to Southeast Asia. Analyse." (typical)

Structure: (1) 1991 origins; (2) phases; (3) 2014 shift; (4) economic: AITIGA, RCEP; (5) connectivity and Northeast; (6) security: Vietnam, Philippines, Malabar, IPOI; (7) gaps and way forward. Add a one-line comparison table: Look East = economics, ASEAN; Act East = strategy, wider Indo-Pacific.

quiz.q: India's Look East Policy was launched in:
quiz.w: Under P.V. Narasimha Rao, after the 1991 reforms.

quiz.q: The Act East Policy was announced by Modi at:
quiz.w: At the 12th ASEAN-India Summit in Nay Pyi Taw, November 2014.

quiz.q: India's full ASEAN dialogue partnership began in:
quiz.w: Sectoral partner 1992, full dialogue partner 1996, summit-level 2002.

quiz.q: India withdrew from RCEP negotiations in:
India's first export of the BrahMos missile was to:
quiz.w: A deal of about $375 million, signed in January 2022.

quiz.q: Who wrote 'Constructing a Security Community in Southeast Asia'?
The Mekong–Ganga Cooperation was set up in:
Which state became ASEAN's 11th member in October 2025?
The 'Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative' was announced in:
quiz.w: At the East Asia Summit in Bangkok, November 2019.
